newsitem.title: USA: GM eyes speeding up bids for EDS work - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: GM eyes speeding up bids for EDS work - WSJ.

text.p: General Motors Corp may move faster than previously announced to put to bid data processing jobs now done by Electronic Data Systems Corp, The Wall Street Journal said Tuesday.

GM and EDS previously said that by 2005, the auto maker could put out to competitive bid 25 percent of the roughly $4 billion in annual computer systems work that EDS had monopolized as a GM unit, the story said.
But GM's chief information officer Ralph Szygenda is quoted in the story as saying he wants to move faster than that.

Under agreements signed last year when GM spun EDS off, Szygenda said GM may seek competitive bids on about $60 million of EDS data processing contracts this year, about $250 million in work in 1998 and another $250 million in 1999, the story said.
Szygenda also told the Journal GM is not obliged to give EDS any new data processing business.
